Origin prefix accepts a different authority; actual profile action and same-site hostile delegated prefix host can preserve Lax credentials, while arbitrary cross-site POST may not. Exact supplied-Origin equality repairs that local witness, not missing-Origin/Referer/proxy/CORS/all CSRF. reviews.security_reason: Someone retaining another previously authenticated bearer session can continue as the password-changing user without the new password under old unexpired/login/MFA state. This need not be anonymous access or control over the password-setting request. After requires a second admitted request already holding that different session before revocation; ordinary per-ID locking does not lock it when another ID changes the password.
reviews.negative_reason: After deletes other stored rows by username, preserving only the current session ID, and the matched caller commits. But unchanged DbSession._save queries by ID and creates a fresh SessionObject(id=self.id) when absent, copying its in-memory _data. Named CherryPy18.8.0 saves loaded sessions before finalization; locks are keyed separately by ID, so request B can load old authenticated data, request A can commit password/revocation, then B can reinsert and commit that old ID. Under admitted SQLite+pysqlite/SQLAlchemy1.4.41 with no DML before A commits, CPython3.10.8 explicitly does not BEGIN on SELECT; the retained SQLite setup enables WAL and autoflush=False. Thus no invented universal read-snapshot/lock failure blocks this conditional schedule. Subsequent B lookup can authenticate again. This is residual revocation failure, not introduced authentication or proof every database/isolation interleaving succeeds. Defer paired-negative use rather than certify all old sessions invalid.
reviews.subset_reason: Old session-survival boundary is supported, but matched after persistence/locking/runtime contracts establish a conditional loaded-session resurrection path. Keep explicit residual after-contract failure and unestablished selected negative; do not silently classify it as mere missing context or a new old security issue.
